messages:
Maria C.: Hey all — noticed something weird in the multi-region failover run from earlier. When we drain eu-west, tail latency spikes in us-east for a small subset of queries (~2-3%), but only when kernel selector is toggled to 'auto'.

Ajay: Hmm. spike meaning p95 jumps or p99?

Maria C.: p95 up ~40ms, p99 up ~180ms for affected traces. Most requests fine. Happens on requests that hit heavy KV cache miss + long context (>1k tokens).

Sam W.: Does it reproduce with replay harness or only synthetic?

Maria C.: Repro with replay (scaled) and with synth traffic that mimics arrival shape. Not with very small short sequences.

Jen L.: Any logs showing kernel switch events during the spike window?

Maria C.: Yes — here's a clipped log from the runtime agent during the drain:

```
2026-03-15T10:12:41Z [route=us-east] incoming req id=abc123 seq=1200 tokens=1120 kv_hit=false
2026-03-15T10:12:41Z [kernel-pick] selected_kernel=compact_float16 reason=auto_profile
2026-03-15T10:12:41Z [kv] miss primed=false
2026-03-15T10:12:42Z [fallback] switched_kernel=compact_int8 reason=underutilized-kernel
2026-03-15T10:12:42Z [latency] tail=312ms
```

Ajay: So auto_profile picked float16, then fallback to int8 mid-request? That handoff could be blowing the KV pointers or causing extra recompute.

Kai: mid-request kernel handoff is supposed to be safe but we haven't exercised it much with KV misses + long seq. Could be cache priming race.

Sam W.: What batching heuristics were used in that run? Continuous batching with 50ms window?

Maria C.: We used default: adaptive batching (latency SLO 100ms, max batch 64, 30ms gather window under low util). During drift it widened to 60ms briefly.

Jen L.: Can you re-run with kernel selection pinned to `compact_int8` and `compact_float16` separately, same arrival shape? Quick A/B to isolate.

Maria C.: Will do. Re-ran pinned int8 and float16. Results:
- pinned int8: no p99 spikes (stable)
- pinned float16: p99 spikes persist and are worse

perf-bot: load-test summary uploaded: https://ci.redwood/tests/2132109/report

Ajay: That strongly suggests an issue in the auto->fallback path when starting on float16. Maybe kernel change triggers a different memory layout for KV cache priming.

Kai: I can instrument the kernel-switch path to emit GC/alloc counts and a KV pointer sanity check. Also add a tiny probe that refuses mid-request switching if kv_miss=true and seq_len>1024.

Sam W.: Also capture batching boundary times and whether the request moved between worker threads during fallback. Thread migration + different kernel could add boundary cost.

Maria C.: I'll run an apples-to-apples replay with: (a) pinned int8, (b) pinned float16, (c) auto but disable mid-request switching (patch Kai suggested). Keep same seed and arrival shape.

Jen L.: Add a metric to Console: `kernel_switch_mid_req{kv_miss="true", seq_len=">1024"}` so we can filter traces in dashboards.

Maria C.: Will push experiments and share links. Early diff shows 30% fewer p99 spikes with the mid-request-disable patch.

Ajay: Good. If that holds, we should consider changing the default heuristic: avoid mid-request kernel switches for requests hitting cold KV and long context. Make it opt-in in `auto` mode for now.

Kai: Filed: ENG-RUNTIME-5789 (instrument kernel switch, add guard, add metric).

Sam W.: Also note for the run notes: region drain increases likelihood of warm->cold KV transitions because of traffic shuffling. Put that in the multi-region methodology doc.

Maria C.: Agreed — adding to the benchmark methodology checklist: replicate drain-induced cache churn, include long-context KV-miss percent as a knob, and include kernel-switch tracing.

Jen L.: Thanks everyone. Ping me once the replay results are in and we'll discuss rollout plan for the conservative heuristic. :+1:
